lessonTitle: Interpreting Common Blood Tests: U&E, Liver Tests and Troponin

blocks.text: A 24-year-old returns from a trek with three days of watery diarrhoea. Her urea is high but her creatinine is only slightly above her usual value. The two numbers come from the same kidney, yet they tell different stories, and learning to read the gap between them is the heart of interpreting a blood test.

blocks.markdown: A urea and electrolytes (U&E) panel measures sodium, potassium, urea and creatinine, often with bicarbonate and an estimated glomerular filtration rate (eGFR). **Creatinine** is produced steadily from muscle and filtered by the glomerulus, so its serum level rises when GFR falls; it also depends on muscle mass, so the same value means different kidney function in a frail older woman and a muscular young man. **Urea** is made in the liver from protein breakdown, is filtered and partly reabsorbed in the tubules (more so when the patient is dehydrated), and is raised by high protein intake, gastrointestinal bleeding and some drugs as well as by kidney impairment.

rows: Pre-renal (low perfusion, dehydration), gastrointestinal bleeding, high protein intake
Tubular reabsorption of urea increases with volume depletion
Reduced GFR from intrinsic renal or post-renal causes
Compare with baseline to distinguish acute from chronic
Reduced renal excretion, acidosis, cell breakdown, spurious (haemolysis)
Risk of arrhythmia; check ECG if significantly raised
Water excess or sodium loss; assess volume status
Interpret with osmolality and clinical state
blocks.caption: Reading a U&E (reference ranges vary by laboratory).

blocks.markdown: **Acute kidney injury (AKI)** is recognised by a rise in serum creatinine of at least 26 micromol/L within 48 hours, or to at least 1.5 times baseline within 7 days, or by a fall in urine output. The KDIGO stages are 1 (1.5 to 1.9 times baseline), 2 (2.0 to 2.9 times) and 3 (3.0 times or more, or creatinine above 354 micromol/L). Chronic kidney disease is persistent reduction in eGFR for at least 3 months.

blocks.title: Staging AKI from creatinine
blocks.prompt: A patient's baseline creatinine is 70 micromol/L. On admission with an infection it is 150 micromol/L. Calculate the ratio and stage the AKI.

steps.text: Compare with KDIGO bands: 2.0 to 2.9 times baseline is stage 2.
The absolute rise (80 micromol/L) also exceeds 26 micromol/L, consistent with AKI.

blocks.markdown: **Liver function tests (LFTs)** include aminotransferases (ALT, AST, enzymes released from damaged hepatocytes), alkaline phosphatase (ALP) and gamma-glutamyl transferase (GGT), made in bile duct epithelium and raised in cholestasis, bilirubin and albumin. A **hepatocellular** pattern has a disproportionate rise in ALT and AST (for example viral hepatitis, paracetamol overdose). A **cholestatic** pattern has a disproportionate rise in ALP and GGT with raised conjugated bilirubin and pale stools, dark urine and itching (for example gallstone obstruction or primary biliary cholangitis). Albumin and prothrombin time reflect synthetic function, not injury.

blocks.caption: ULN is the upper limit of normal. R above 5 suggests hepatocellular injury, below 2 cholestatic, and between 2 and 5 a mixed pattern.

blocks.title: Calculating the R ratio
blocks.prompt: A patient has ALT 220 U/L (ULN 40 U/L) and ALP 300 U/L (ULN 130 U/L). Calculate R and classify the pattern.

steps.text: ALT as a multiple of ULN.
ALP as a multiple of ULN.
R between 2 and 5 is a mixed pattern.

blocks.answer: R is about 2.4: a mixed hepatocellular and cholestatic pattern.

blocks.markdown: **Troponin.** Cardiac troponins I and T are structural proteins of cardiomyocytes released when the cells are damaged. They are highly specific for myocardial injury. After an infarct, high-sensitivity troponin begins to rise within 1 to 3 hours, peaks at about 12 to 24 hours and remains elevated for about 7 to 14 days. Diagnosis uses a rise and/or fall of troponin with at least one value above the 99th percentile upper reference limit, together with symptoms, ECG changes or imaging. Because a single early sample may be normal, serial measurements are used. Troponin is also raised in myocarditis, pulmonary embolism, sepsis and renal failure, so a raised level shows myocardial injury, not necessarily myocardial infarction.

blocks.title: Context matters
blocks.text: A single abnormal number is a prompt for interpretation, not a diagnosis. Always compare with baseline, consider drugs, muscle mass, hydration and sample quality, and repeat when the result does not fit the clinical picture.

points: Compare creatinine with baseline to detect AKI (KDIGO stages by ratio); a disproportionate rise in urea points to pre-renal causes or bleeding.
Hepatocellular injury raises ALT and AST; cholestasis raises ALP and GGT with conjugated bilirubin; the R ratio helps classify.
Troponin is specific for myocardial injury, rises within hours, and stays elevated for 7 to 14 days, so serial testing is needed.

questions.stem: Which U&E pattern most suggests pre-renal azotaemia?

options.text: Urea raised proportionately more than creatinine
Creatinine raised with a normal urea
Both normal with a high sodium

questions.correctOptionText: Urea raised proportionately more than creatinine

distractorRationale.a: Correct: with volume depletion more urea is reabsorbed in the tubule.
distractorRationale.b: This is not the typical pattern.
distractorRationale.c: Low urea suggests low protein intake or liver disease.
distractorRationale.d: This does not indicate reduced GFR.

questions.explanation: When circulating volume is low, tubular reabsorption of urea increases, raising urea disproportionately. Creatinine is reabsorbed less, so it rises less.

questions.stem: A 72-year-old man with difficulty passing urine has creatinine 380 micromol/L (baseline 85) and potassium 6.4 mmol/L. What is the most important immediate concern from the potassium?

distractorRationale.a: Correct: hyperkalaemia alters cardiac conduction and can cause arrhythmia.

questions.explanation: Reduced GFR in AKI limits potassium excretion, and a level of 6.4 mmol/L carries a risk of ECG changes and arrhythmia. It needs prompt assessment, including an ECG.

questions.stem: A patient has markedly raised ALP and GGT, raised conjugated bilirubin, pale stools and itch, but only a mildly raised ALT. Which pattern is this?

distractorRationale.b: Hepatocellular has ALT and AST dominant.
distractorRationale.d: Haemolysis has unconjugated bilirubin and normal ALP.

questions.explanation: Raised ALP and GGT with conjugated hyperbilirubinaemia and pale stools indicate obstruction to bile flow. Itch comes from bile salt retention.

questions.stem: A 31-year-old has ALT 900 U/L, AST 750 U/L and normal ALP. Which cause best fits this pattern?

options.text: Gallstone in the common bile duct

distractorRationale.a: Correct: marked aminotransferase rise with little ALP rise is hepatocellular.
distractorRationale.d: This causes obstruction and a cholestatic pattern.

questions.explanation: A strong rise in ALT and AST with a normal ALP is a hepatocellular pattern. Viral hepatitis and drug toxicity are typical causes.

questions.stem: A man arrives 90 minutes after the onset of chest pain and his first high-sensitivity troponin is below the 99th percentile. What is the best interpretation?

options.text: Myocardial infarction is not excluded and a repeat sample is needed
Infarction is excluded and he can be discharged
The troponin is falsely low and should be ignored

questions.correctOptionText: Myocardial infarction is not excluded and a repeat sample is needed

distractorRationale.a: Correct: troponin may not have risen yet.
distractorRationale.b: Early normal results do not exclude infarction.
distractorRationale.c: The test is not necessarily false, only too early.
distractorRationale.d: There is no basis for this.

questions.explanation: Troponin starts to rise 1 to 3 hours after injury, so an early sample may be negative. Serial measurements show the rise or fall required for the diagnosis.

questions.stem: After a myocardial infarction, troponin may remain elevated for about 1 to 2 weeks.
questions.explanation: Cardiac troponin has a long window of persistence, about 7 to 14 days. This makes it useful for late presentation but unsuitable for detecting reinfarction soon after.

questions.stem: A patient's baseline creatinine is 90 micromol/L and it is now 144 micromol/L. Calculate the ratio of current to baseline creatinine (dimensionless). KDIGO stage 1 is 1.5 to 1.9 times baseline.
questions.explanation: The ratio is 144 divided by 90, which is 1.6. This falls within the stage 1 band, so AKI stage 1 applies.

questions.stem: A patient has ALT 600 U/L (ULN 40 U/L) and ALP 180 U/L (ULN 120 U/L). Calculate the R ratio (dimensionless). R above 5 indicates a hepatocellular pattern.
questions.explanation: ALT is 15 times ULN and ALP is 1.5 times ULN, so R is 15 divided by 1.5, which is 10. This is greater than 5, so the pattern is hepatocellular.

questions.stem: A 68-year-old man with vomiting for 4 days has Na 131 mmol/L, K 5.9 mmol/L, urea 26 mmol/L and creatinine 260 micromol/L (baseline 85). Interpret the U&E and explain what you would do next.
markingGuide: Creatinine about three times baseline: AKI KDIGO stage 3 ratio
Urea disproportionately raised suggests pre-renal cause or volume depletion
Hyperkalaemia from reduced excretion needs ECG and prompt management
Assess fluid status and urine output
questions.explanation: The creatinine ratio gives severity, the urea to creatinine relationship suggests mechanism, and potassium determines urgency. Marking should reward systematic interpretation.

questions.stem: Explain the time course of troponin after myocardial infarction and how it is used in suspected infarction. Give two other causes of a raised troponin.
markingGuide: Specific protein of cardiomyocytes released on injury
Remains raised for about 7 to 14 days
Diagnosis needs a rise and/or fall with a value above the 99th percentile
Serial samples because an early value may be normal
Other causes: myocarditis, pulmonary embolism, sepsis or renal failure
questions.explanation: Troponin shows myocardial injury, and the pattern of change plus the clinical context identifies infarction. The long persistence limits its use for reinfarction.
